Senator Angus King used his round at the Senate Veterans' Affairs oversight hearing to press VA Secretary Doug Collins for the list of 585 canceled VA contracts he had requested in a letter two months earlier. King said the response he received on Friday did not include the list, and when Collins said the contracts were still being renegotiated, King said the refusal made him wonder if there are things in those contracts Collins does not want the committee to know about. Collins said that was not the case and that his team was working through it, but he would not commit when King proposed next Friday, prompting King to call the answer really not very satisfactory and the antithesis of transparency. King then challenged the plan to return VA staffing to 2019 levels as an arbitrary quota rather than an efficiency analysis, and closed by asking whether Collins will share the department's review data with the committee.

Did King make his case that the contract list should be public, or is Collins right to wait? Share your thoughts below.
youtube.videoTitle: "WHY WON'T YOU TELL US WHAT THOSE CONTRACTS ARE?": Angus King vs. Doug Collins #Shorts
